solutionSteps: Let the circumcentre be $O(x, y)$. Since $O$ is equidistant from all vertices: $OA^2 = OB^2 = OC^2$.

questions.question: If one diagonal of a square is along the line $8x - 15y = 0$ and one of its vertices is at $(1, 2)$, find the equations of the sides of the square passing through this vertex.
solutionSteps: The diagonal line $8x - 15y = 0$ does not pass through $(1, 2)$ because $8(1) - 15(2) = -22 \ne 0$.
In a square, the sides make an angle of $45^\circ$ with either diagonal.
Let $m$ be the slope of a side: $\tan 45^\circ = \left|\frac{m - 8/15}{1 + 8m/15}\right| = 1$.
